title: Runtime compatibility and behavioral contracts for hosted inference surface
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define the behavioral contracts, runtime compatibility matrix, and gated acceptance criteria for the hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). This ticket bundles the product-level decisions needed to (1) guarantee predictable API behavior across model variants and runtime optimizations, (2) specify acceptable failure and degraded modes, and (3) provide a deterministic rollout and go/no-go checklist for launch.

Background: Multiple engineering efforts are moving toward a converged hosted surface that supports streaming, structured output, and function/tool-calling. The runtime team introduced kernel selection heuristics and quantized variants that alter latency/cost characteristics. Without a clear contract, customers can observe inconsistent output shape, different temperature/penalty semantics, or latency spikes when automatic fallbacks occur. This PRD locks down the user-visible guarantees and release gates so downstream SDKs, docs, billing, and support can align.

Scope (in): behavioral API-level guarantees for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank; model-to-variant mapping table; streaming and non-streaming parity definitions; default fallback semantics across tiers; observability and SLO definitions; canary rollout plan and rollback triggers; acceptance tests and gating checklist.

Scope (out): model training changes, research model architecture changes, major new model additions (these get separate onboarding tickets), dedicated capacity autoscaler tuning (handled by Dedicated team), on-prem packaging details.

Key decisions made so far: 1) Single behavioral contract per surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) that enforces consistent tokenization, default sampling semantics, and structured-output schema stability across model variants. 2) Streaming parity: streaming responses must always be prefix-consistent with non-streaming responses for the same request; we accept up to 50ms additional per-chunk latency introduced by runtime batching. 3) Fallback behavior: define three-tier fallback mapping (primary -> soft-fallback -> hard-fallback) with documented model flavor differences and automated notification to the console when soft-fallbacks exceed 0.5% of traffic. 4) Regional routing: payloads with explicit data_residency tags are pinned to regionally compatible runtime nodes; cross-region fallback only allowed with customer opt-in. 5) Quantized variants: output quality regression threshold set at <2% degraded utility on our eval sets; quantized fallback allowed only when latency SLO is breached.

Trade-offs and risks: Tight behavioral contracts limit rapid runtime experimentation and require additional regression signal instrumentation. Allowing quantized variants improves cost but risks subtle quality regressions; mitigations include continuous evals and gated rollouts. Enforcing streaming/non-streaming parity may increase engineering work for special-cased model kernels.

Deliverables: 1) Behavioral contract docs (per-surface) for public docs and SDKs; 2) Runtime compatibility matrix (model family vs supported features); 3) Acceptance test suite (end-to-end smoke and regression tests); 4) Canary and rollout runbook; 5) Dashboards and alerts; 6) Release notes and customer-facing FAQ.
acceptance_criteria: AC-001: For any request sent to /v1/chat or /v1/completions, non-streaming vs streaming responses are byte-prefix-equivalent (ignoring chunk boundaries) for the canonical test prompts in the regression set.
AC-002: Embeddings produced by supported model variants must have cosine similarity >= 0.995 vs reference embeddings on the canonical corpus (per-model thresholds documented in compatibility matrix).

AC-003: Rerank endpoint must return stable ordering for identical inputs within rolling 5-minute windows unless the model variant changes; any deviation must be explainable via release notes and detectable by regression tests.
AC-004: Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for baseline lane and p99 <= 650ms for baseline lane under the defined traffic profile in the acceptance harness.

AC-005: Fallback transparency: when soft-fallbacks occur for >0.5% of requests in canary, console shows alert and automated rollback to previous route is triggered unless acknowledged by on-call within 15 minutes.

AC-006: Security and data residency: requests with data_residency=EU are never routed outside EU without explicit customer opt-in; audited in the acceptance run and test logs are retained for 90 days.

AC-007: End-to-end SDK parity: official JS and Python SDKs demonstrate identical request/response handling for the new surface; integration tests pass in CI with no more than 1 transient failure per 1000 runs.
AC-008: Load and stability: sustained soak at 3x expected launch QPS for 30 minutes must not increase error rate above 1% and must not violate p99 latency SLOs more than 5% of the time.
AC-009: Observability: per-route token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, and a regression alert tied to reference prompts are available in console dashboards and wired into the pager policy.
AC-010: Documentation: public behavioral contract page, SDK changelog, and rollback/runbook must be published before open beta signups are allowed.
launch_checklist: PRDs reviewed and signed-off by Eng, Research, Security, and DX (design/docs)
Compatibility matrix published (model -> features -> runtime limitations)
API spec updated and OpenAPI/JSON schemas published for structured outputs
SDKs updated (python/js) and smoke-tested against canary endpoints
Acceptance tests added to pipeline and green for three consecutive runs
Canary cluster configured: 1% traffic initial, plan for 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours
Canary alert thresholds configured (soft-fallback >0.5%, error rate >0.5%, p99 latency breach) and runbook assigned
Billing/pricing updates coordinated with Finance and legal; cost-estimates for quantized vs full variants published
Customer communication draft ready: FAQ, migration guidance, breaking-changes summary
Support playbook and triage runbook published in Confluence with sample escalations
Dashboard tiles: per-route latency, cost/token, fallback-rate, regional routing failures
E2E performance soak test run at 3x QPS for 30 minutes and results recorded
Regression evals run across canonical prompt set; quality delta <2% for quantized variants
Audit logs and data residency tests executed and stored (90-day retention verified)
Security review completed and required findings mitigated
Rollout toggle created and tested (feature-flag + infra gating)
Rollback tested: revert routing and confirm stateful systems (KV cache) recover within SLO window
Post-launch monitoring: 24/7 watch rotation for first 72 hours and daily retros scheduled
